findings.passage: Pushing out a deputy of eight years and humiliating the beaten add none. They are what a man does when the point is who is in charge.
findings.problem: The repair replaced the discriminator after the jury's review, and the new one is asserted, not shown. No opened source says what Ray Lane's removal or the 'humiliate' conduct did to Ellison's standing, yet the page says they add no admiration and, two paragraphs on, that they buy control 'at the expense of admiration'; FAQ 2 repeats it. Two facts that cut the other way are left off the page. First, reports from July 3, 2000 that open freely (The Register 'Exit Lane', Reuters via Wired 'Ellison Now No. 1 and 2 at Oracle', Computerworld) say Lane resigned, that Oracle gave no reason, that he was 'widely credited' with Oracle's recovery and 'highly regarded by the street', and that Ellison took his titles. Removing the deputy who was getting the credit is what a Three would do, so the act does not separate the types as written. The same reports say Oracle shares fell 4.6 percent on the news, which is the only sourced cost in the episode and is not used. Second, the review that supplies 'he had to humiliate them' (S45) gives Wilson's theme in the same passage: Ellison, like Charles Foster Kane, 'wants desperately to be loved, even idolized', and succeeded 'not as a technologist but as a marketeer'. The page takes the line that helps Type 8 from that source and leaves out the biographer's own reading, which is more direct Type 3 evidence than the passage it calls 'the strongest Type 3 evidence that does not come from Ellison'. In the review the 'humiliate' sentence also follows 'The Oracle Way… was simply to win' and is illustrated by product claims, not by an episode. This is the defect critic-03, enneagram-01 and enneagram-03 raised, moved to new evidence that no reviewer saw.
findings.acceptance_test: The page states, with the three July 2000 reports added as sources, that Lane resigned with no reason given, that he was widely credited with Oracle's recovery, and what his exit cost Ellison, and it gives the Type 3 reading of the removal beside the Type 8 one. It reports Wilson's Citizen Kane theme from S45 wherever it uses the 'humiliate' line. The discriminator is then restated at the strength the sources carry: each episode offered names whose regard was at stake and cites that it was lost, or the page says plainly that no opened evidence separates Type 8 from Type 3 and lowers the stated confidence. The record already holds third-party conduct worth testing for this (S03 introduction: Siebel and Conway on him, and his attack on Wall Street analysts to their faces; S07: 'His own CFO calls him a dictator'). The 60-word answer, FAQs 1 and 2 and the description match the result, the body stays under 4,500 words, and because the deciding argument is new since the frozen review, the revised draft goes through --refresh --expanded-review.

research_tasks: Read Mike Wilson's The Difference Between God and Larry Ellison (1997) and Matthew Symonds's Softwar (2003) in licensed copies. The Internet Archive copies are lending-restricted and its search-inside service returned 'Item not available' on 2026-11-12. In Wilson: find the 'he had to humiliate them' sentence and the episodes behind it, the friend's account of invented stories and who is speaking, and the Citizen Kane theme. In both: who initiated Ray Lane's departure in 2000, whether credit for the recovery was at issue, and Ellison's footnoted reply in Softwar.

Add as sources the reports of July 3, 2000 on Lane's exit, each opened in this verification: theregister.com/2000/07/03/exit_lane ('quit ... unexpectedly'; 'widely credited with the company's rapid growth'); wired.com/2000/07/ellison-now-no-1-and-2-at-oracle (Reuters: Oracle 'declined to comment on why Lane was leaving'; shares down 4.6 percent; Lane 'highly regarded by the street'; Ellison assumes president and COO duties); computerworld.com/article/1378050 ('did not cite a reason'; success 'attributed to Lane'). Use them to state both readings of the removal.

Test third-party conduct already in opened sources as a discriminator: the Playboy introduction (S03) quotes Tom Siebel that he takes 'the best and brightest and then he tries to destroy them' and Craig Conway that 'When you alienate everybody, you become someone no one wants to play with', and describes him attacking Wall Street analysts in the room; Fortune (S07) says 'His own CFO calls him a dictator'; in S03 he says half his senior executives wanted him out over the Internet strategy. Check each in context and say whether it shows him spending the regard of an audience a Three would court.

Use the fuller origin passage in the 1995 oral history (S01, 'A South Side Boy') beside the Kirkus report: he says Look Magazine called the area 'the oldest and worst black ghetto in the United States' and also calls it 'a lower middle class neighborhood' and 'a Jewish ghetto'.

PRE-RELEASE, still open: the Forbes interview of April 2020 (TheWrap and an April 2020 Business Insider report carry the 'devil' sentence; only TheWrap was opened for 'I was not here'); USC's official video of the May 2016 speech for 'That way I could completely control my work environment'; the Washington Post report of May 2022 and the Fair Fight v. True the Vote filing; the Delaware docket for Robbins v. Ellison, No. 2026-0928; Bloomberg Businessweek (June 2022) and the New York Times Magazine (September 2014) on Lanai.

Register the page's controversies in docs/writing-system/people-controversies.json and run pnpm controversies:check. Write the 2013 America's Cup penalty beside the 2013 result. Open the Delaware rulings on the NetSuite purchase and add one paragraph with the outcome and his side's response.
Corroborate the September 1993 SEC settlement and the $24 million shareholder settlement in the SEC release or a newspaper report; the only opened source is one Computergram item.
After the discriminator is revised, run scripts/run-blog-pipeline.sh larry-ellison --refresh --expanded-review so the new type argument gets a full independent jury.

evidence.reason: All 84 quotations on the page match their sources word for word in my re-fetch, and attributions are exact about what was and was not opened ('according to a published transcript', 'quoted by TheWrap', 'this is the reviewers' report'). The court finding is quoted from the opinion. Limits stay visible. What holds it at this level: most of the record is his own testimony, the third-party evidence that now decides the typing arrives secondhand (Wilson through reviews, the reason for Lane's exit through one CBS clause), and two pieces of context at that deciding point are missing (reverify-01).
evidence.passage: Neither that book nor Matthew Symonds's _Softwar_ (2003) was read for this profile, so this is the reviewers' report. It discounts every self-report below and counts for Type 3.

enneagram.reason: The alternative is tested harder than on most type pages: Type 3 gets its own section built from his words, the rank evidence, Grove and the embellishment reports, and the page concedes that public conduct cannot separate the two. Type 6 is tested on behaviour and no wing or arrow is used to absorb a contradiction. But the step that is supposed to put Type 8 ahead is one unshown sentence. The page itself says no source shows what his defiance cost him, and the two new exhibits do not show admiration and control pulling apart; contemporaneous reports give Lane's removal a ready Type 3 reading, and the biographer quoted for 'humiliate' reads him as wanting to be 'loved, even idolized'. The alternative does not fail a specific, sourced discriminator, so this sits below the standard's anchor for 8.
enneagram.passage: Type 8 still leads, at medium confidence, because the conduct others report buys control at the expense of admiration.

originality.reason: The frame is specific to him and I have not seen it elsewhere: one story told twice with 'admired' in one telling and 'respected' in the other, both verified. Other details are just as particular, including the correction of the Genghis Khan line from his own 1995 account, the 1,000-year vow, a father's trust in government reappearing in the son's surveillance remarks, and the check of his 'still worse neighborhood' joke against what reviewers say the biography found. Type boilerplate is limited to one short triad paragraph.
originality.passage: Admired in one telling, respected in the other. It could be a slip of memory forty years on. It is also the open question about him.

writing.reason: The first half moves well: the two tellings, the founding quotation, the fear answer read sentence by sentence, and the storm section with its closing line. The second half reads more like a brief. The Type 3 section ends in three bolded evidence blocks, the last third is a run of controversies each closed by a short disclaimer, and the page stops to describe its own method several times ('was not read for this profile', 'was not audited here'). At 4,487 words it is at the ceiling and about a thousand over the target, and the ending earns its place only after that stretch.
writing.passage: It is a joke. It also reads as an accurate self-portrait: a man who met a real limit, respected it, and still left himself an opening.

durability.reason: The argument rests on dated material from 1995 to 2010, and deleting everything after 2016 leaves the hook, the type sections and the ending intact. Changing facts carry absolute dates and review triggers (roles as of November 2026, the pending suit, the guarantee). It loses ground on the 2013 Cup result stated without the penalty, five checks left for before publication, one dated fact with no trigger, and a typing the record itself marks unresolved until two old books are read.
durability.passage: These are claims in a complaint. As of November 2026, no ruling on them had been found for this profile.

hook.reason: It opens on a sourced contradiction in his own telling, gives both versions in his words with outlet and date, admits the dull explanation, and turns the one-word difference into the question the page then tests. The ending returns to it and says honestly that the word never settled.
hook.passage: Larry Ellison has told the same story about his sister at least twice, and the key word changes.

discoverability.reason: Meta title is 55 characters and the description 169. The type heading is followed by a 58-word plain answer that FAQ 1 mirrors. Seven FAQs answer real searches (the 'everyone else must fail' quotation, insider trading, the 1998 race, his Oracle role) and every anchor matches a heading. Internal links go to the Type 8, 3 and 6 pages and to Gates, Musk and Jobs, all of which exist. FAQ 2 and the 1998 FAQ will need to follow the repairs in reverify-01 and reverify-04.
discoverability.passage: Larry Ellison is best read as an Enneagram Type 8, the Challenger, at medium confidence. He names control as his motive and does not retreat under criticism.
